title: Roman numerals: read the small pieces first
description: Turn a string like MCMXLIV into manageable parts, with a short practice set to check yourself.

sections.title: Seven symbols are enough to begin
sections.html:
A date carved over a doorway can look forbidding until you stop reading it as one long word. Roman numerals use a small set of symbols. For the common forms you meet in quizzes, start here:

I = 1 · V = 5 · X = 10 · L = 50
C = 100 · D = 500 · M = 1,000

Read VI as five plus one: six. Read VIII as five plus three: eight. Build a little confidence with those before tackling a building date.

sections.title: Look for the subtraction pairs
sections.html:
In standard modern notation, a smaller symbol before an appropriate larger one can form a subtraction pair. The familiar pairs are IV (4), IX (9), XL (40), XC (90), CD (400) and CM (900).

This is not permission to put any small symbol before any large one. Write 49 as XLIX: forty plus nine. IL is not the standard form. Historical inscriptions and clock faces can use variants, including IIII for four, so a real object may not follow a school exercise exactly.

sections.title: A doorway date, one chunk at a time
sections.html:
Try MCMXLIV. Separate it into M | CM | XL | IV. You now have 1,000 + 900 + 40 + 4, which gives 1944. Each chunk is easier to check than a hurried running total.

For a second pass, go backwards: build 1944 from thousands, hundreds, tens and units. If the pieces match, you have checked the reading without merely repeating the same mental step.

What is MMXXVI?

2026: MM is 2,000, XX is 20 and VI is 6. There are no subtraction pairs in this example.

sections.title: Three small checks
sections.html:
On paper, try XIV, XLII and XC. Before opening the answers, circle any subtraction pair. Then read the remaining symbols normally.

Show the three answers

XIV = 14; XLII = 42; XC = 90. In XIV, only IV is the subtraction pair: the initial X still contributes ten.

Next time a quiz includes a Roman numeral, look for a familiar pair first. You do not need to hold the whole string in memory.
